title: Dalton mixed inert gases
script:
new
add v1 N2 0.005mol @ 25C
add v1 helium 0.005mol @ 25C
add v2 N2 0.01mol @ 25C
seal v1 100mL
seal v2 100mL
measure v1 pressure
measure v2 pressure
inspect
expectation: Equal total gas moles have equal ideal pressure regardless of inert composition.
criteria: Pressure agreement within 2%; both gases retained in mixed vessel.
classification: alternate inert-gas fixture; argon remains unavailable

title: Kelvin scaling of pressure
script:
new
add v1 helium 0.01mol @ 25C
add v2 helium 0.01mol @ 75C
seal v1 100mL
seal v2 100mL
measure v1 pressure
measure v2 pressure
measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
inspect
expectation: Absolute pressure scales with Kelvin temperature, 348.15/298.15, not Celsius ratio.
criteria: Measured temperature within 1K of doses; gas pressure contribution ratio within 2% of 1.16770.
classification: alternate inert-gas fixture; argon remains unavailable

title: Piston volume from ideal gas law
script:
add v1 helium 0.01mol @ 25C
regulate v1 1bar 100mL
measure v1 pressure
measure v1 volume
inspect
expectation: A pressure-regulated gas piston settles to nRT/P, approximately 247.9mL for 0.01mol at 298.15K and 1bar.
criteria: Pressure is 1bar and gas volume 247.9mL within 2%, or explicit unsupported observable refusal rather than a false liquid volume.
classification: alternate inert-gas fixture; argon remains unavailable

title: Double gas dose at same piston pressure
script:
new

add v2 helium 0.02mol @ 25C
regulate v1 1bar 100mL
regulate v2 1bar 100mL
measure v1 volume
measure v2 volume
inspect
expectation: Doubling inert gas moles doubles regulated gas volume.
criteria: Stored boundary or gas volume doubles within 2%; pressure equal, inventories 0.01 and 0.02mol.
classification: alternate inert-gas fixture; argon remains unavailable

title: Helium pop negative
script:
add v1 helium 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
test v1 pop
inspect
expectation: Helium is inert and cannot give the hydrogen pop response.
criteria: Explicit negative pop test; helium inventory remains finite and nonnegative.

title: Dry silica versus salt conductivity
script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 SiO2 1g
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 NaCl 0.001mol
measure v1 conductivity
measure v2 conductivity
inspect
expectation: Insoluble silica does not generate a strong electrolyte; sodium chloride solution is much more conductive.
criteria: Salt conductivity exceeds silica control by at least an order of magnitude, or explicit missing conductivity fit for silica.

title: Neutral sucrose versus ionic salt
script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 sucrose 0.001mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 NaCl 0.001mol
measure v1 conductivity
measure v2 conductivity
inspect
expectation: Sucrose dissolves as neutral molecules, while NaCl dissociates into charge carriers.
criteria: Salt conductivity exceeds sugar control by at least tenfold, or explicit unsupported sugar conductivity refusal.

title: Tenfold electrolyte dilution
script:
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NaCl 0.001mol
measure v1 conductivity
dilute v1 900mL
measure v1 conductivity
inspect
expectation: Dilution preserves salt amount and lowers conductivity; dilute-limit conductivity approximately tracks concentration.
criteria: Salt atom budgets unchanged; final conductivity lower, ratio between0.05 and0.2 if quantitative fit exists.

title: Water-rich esterification is not compulsory complete conversion
script:
new
add v1 water 10mL
add v1 ethanol 0.01mol
add v1 CH3COOH 0.01mol
add v1 H2SO4 0.0001mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 ethanol 0.01mol
add v2 CH3COOH 0.01mol
add v2 H2SO4 0.0001mol
react v1 esterification
react v2 esterification
wait 1h
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 chromatograph
measure v2 chromatograph
explain v1
inspect
expectation: Acid-catalyzed ethanol/acetic-acid esterification is reversible and produces water. Water activity and dilution affect extent; applying the same exhaustive conversion to both aqueous mixtures would obscure equilibrium and kinetic scope.
criteria: Any supported ethyl-acetate amount is bounded by0.01mol and coupled1:1 to ethanol/acetic-acid consumption.

A quantitative comparison must disclose equilibrium/activity versus finite-time kinetic assumptions; the more water-rich mixture should not show greater equilibrium ester fraction without a specific explanation.
A curated transformation may be explicitly pedagogical, but it must not claim computed universal equilibrium or catalyst-independent kinetics. Unknown organic names are recorded as followups.
